note: Shares of valid, non-permanent-water 20 m land pixels in percent: likely new open water (water_pct), likely wet or flooded crops (crops_pct), total_pct = both. normal_pct = water+crops share for the normal pair 4-16 Oct with the same thresholds; change_vs_normal_pp = total_pct - normal_pct. *_err = largest shift when the change threshold moves by +/-1 sigma. rank = by total_pct (likely flooded = water + crops) among mandals with >=50% valid coverage and >=50% of the mandal inside the footprint; rank_water = by water_pct only (use this for headlines: the wet-crops class is not separable from normal field change, docs/METHODS.md); null = flagged, not ranked. area_km2 = valid non-permanent-water land seen by the radar; water_km2, crops_km2, flooded_km2 = share x area. Top-level rows = newest date; oct28 = the landfall-day scene; by_date holds every coast date after the baseline. 9 Nov combines Arnab (27-28 Oct), Murasu (1-3 Nov) and the river peak.

provenance.credit: NISAR L2 GCOV, NASA/JPL-Caltech and ISRO, via ASF DAAC (NASA Earthdata)
provenance.method: L-band HH+HV on the 20 m coast grid; 3x3 boxcar in linear power; baseline = mean of the two pre-event dates; permanent water = HH below the water threshold on both baseline dates (excluded); new water = HH and HV both fall by >= 3 sigma and HH ends below the threshold; wet crops = HH rises >= 3 sigma and HV >= 1 sigma and not water; shares are of valid, non-permanent-water land pixels inside each mandal polygon. See docs/METHODS.md.
caveats: single band (L); S-band not used yet
baseline scenes 4 and 16 Oct are PROVISIONAL products
no ground truth: classes are radar-only and not validated against a flood map
speckle: 20 m pixels are noisy, errors show the effect of moving the threshold by one sigma only
9 Nov also reflects Cyclone Murasu (1-3 Nov) and the Godavari peak, not Arnab alone
